name: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex Due to Exophilin 5 Deficiency
aliases: Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex with EXPH5 Mutation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Epidermolysis Bullosa Simplex

criteria.description: Recurrent skin blistering localized to areas of mechanical trauma
Intraepidermal cleavage observed on skin biopsy
Identification of biallelic or heterozygous pathogenic variants in EXPH5 gene
Normal expression of keratin 5 and 14 with altered vesicle trafficking markers

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical blistering plus either histopathological confirmation of intraepidermal cleavage or identification of pathogenic EXPH5 variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is critical due to phenotypic overlap with other EBS subtypes.

pathognomonic.notes: Blisters typically arise on hands and feet after minor trauma
searchTerms: blisters inside the skin layer caused by friction

pathognomonic.notes: Erosions heal without significant scarring or milia formation
searchTerms: skin breaks that heal without scars

common.notes: Thickening of skin on palms and soles
Occasional itching localized to affected areas
Wounds may take longer than usual to re-epithelialize

searchTerms: excessive sweating on hands and feet
overactive sweat glands in hands and feet

occasional.notes: Lightened skin patches following blister resolution

rare.notes: Localized hair loss due to repeated blistering on scalp
Resulting from chronic blistering and healing
searchTerms: stiff or bent fingers or toes

rare.symptomName: Anemia secondary to chronic skin loss
rare.notes: Rare complication due to chronic skin breakdown
searchTerms: low red blood cells from chronic skin loss
anemia due to ongoing skin damage

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests except possible anemia in chronic cases
other: Immunofluorescence mapping demonstrating normal keratin 5/14 but altered vesicle trafficking

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in KRT5 or KRT14 genes
Similar blistering but with characteristic keratin cytoskeletal abnormalities
Associated with gastrointestinal symptoms such as pyloric stenosis

redFlags: Signs of systemic infection or sepsis
references: Fine JD, et al. Inherited epidermolysis bullosa: updated recommendations on diagnosis and classification. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2014.
Has C, et al. Exophilin-5 deficiency causes a novel form of epidermolysis bullosa simplex. J Invest Dermatol. 2017.
Orphanet: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex due to exophilin 5 deficiency. ORPHA:412189.
